Arabic | budget = $60 million | gross = $128 million }} '''''A Perfect Murder''''' is a 1998 American [[crime film|crime]] [[thriller film]] directed by [[Andrew Davis (director)|Andrew Davis]] and written by Patrick Smith Kelly. It stars [[Michael Douglas]], [[Gwyneth Paltrow]], and [[Viggo Mortensen]]. It is a remake of the 1954 film ''[[Dial M for Murder]].''{{Cite web |last=Harari |first=Julia |date=2022-06-13 |title=How 'A Perfect Murder' Updated Hitchcock's 'Dial M for Murder' |url=https://collider.com/dial-m-for-murder-a-perfect-murder-remake-comparisons/ |access-date=2025-12-03 |website=Collider |language=en}} ==Plot== [[Wall Street]] [[Stock trader|trader]] Steven Taylor is married to the much younger and wealthy Emily. Meanwhile, a smitten Emily is having an affair with artist David Shaw, for whom she considers leaving Steven. One day, Steven arrives at David's art studio. Steven not only knows about the affair, but has researched David's past. His real identity is Winston Lagrange, an ex-convict who cons rich women. Pointing out that he can easily return him to prison, Steven recruits David into murdering Emily for $500,000, paying him $100,000 in advance. Steven takes Emily's housekey and hides it outside the service entrance to their lavish [[Manhattan]] co-op apartment. David is to use the key to enter the apartment, kill her, and make it appear as a robbery gone bad. At his weekly card game, Steven takes a break and uses his cellphone to call an automated bank system, confirming his alibi, while using a second phone to call Emily. Emily answers in the kitchen and is attacked by a masked assailant, but she fatally stabs him in the neck with a [[meat thermometer]]. Steven returns and finds the assailant's body and a distraught Emily, who has called 911. Working quickly, Steven takes the key from the body, puts it back on Emily's keychain and damages the service entrance door with a screwdriver, then plants it on the assailant. The [[NYPD]] arrives, led by Detective Moe Karaman. They remove the assailant's mask, but the body is not David's. The next day, Steven contacts David, who explains he hired someone he knows from prison to commit the murder, as he did not think he could do it. Emily notices that the key on her ring does not fit the apartment's lock. Suspicious, she confides to her friend that Steven would have inherited her entire $100 million fortune if she had been killed. She makes discrete inquiries and learns that Steven's extremely risky [[margin trading|margin trade]]s on the [[stock market]] are unraveling. If he is unable to find enough capital to cover the balance, both Steven's finances and his credit will be completely wiped out. Detective Karaman tells Emily that no housekey was found on the assailant's body. Soon after, David calls Steven and plays an audio tape of the two [[criminal conspiracy|discussing the plan to kill]] Emily. They meet at a local deli, where David demands the full $500,000 or he will turn Steven in. Emily visits the assailant's apartment to check if the key on her ring fits the lock, which it does. When she confronts Steven, he explains that David is [[blackmail]]ing them and he has been paying him off to stop seeing Emily. When he saw her dead assailant in their kitchen, he assumed it was David, who had threatened to use violence before, and took the key from his pocket to shield Emily from facing murder charges. Steven insists that they are not to call the police as he has tampered with evidence. Steven gives David the money, then follows him onto an Amtrak train and kills him, taking the money and David's gun. As he dies, a laughing David reveals he mailed the tape to Emily via courier service. Steven rushes home and finds the mail still unopened. He hides the money, gun, and audio tape in his safe before showering. Emily asks Steven if they should change the locks, as her key is still missing. Steven retrieves the key from where he hid it and attempts to plant it somewhere else, but Emily sees him. She explains the assailant must have returned the key to the hiding place after opening the door. She reveals she knows everything, having found the tape in the safe and listened to it while he showered. As she turns away, Steven attacks her, vowing she will only leave him dead. After a brief fight, Emily grabs David's gun from the safe and kills Steven. NYPD Detective Karaman later comforts a heartbroken Emily, telling her not to blame herself, as she had no choice but to kill Steven in [[self-defense]]. ==Cast== {{cast listing| * [[Michael Douglas]] as Steven Taylor * [[Gwyneth Paltrow]] as Emily Bradford Taylor * [[Viggo Mortensen]] as David Shaw * [[David Suchet]] as Detective Mohamed "Moe" Karaman * [[Sarita Choudhury]] as Raquel Martinez * [[Constance Towers]] as Sandra Bradford * [[Novella Nelson]] as Ambassador Alice Wills * [[Michael P. Moran]] as Bobby Fain * [[Gerry Becker]] as Roger Brill * [[Will Lyman]] as Jason Gates * [[David Eigenberg]] as Stein }} ==Comparisons to the original film== {{Unreferenced section|date=December 2014}} In Hitchcock's ''Dial M for Murder'', the characters played by [[Ray Milland]] and [[Grace Kelly]] are depicted as living in a modest London flat, although it is implied that they are quite wealthy, as Milland's character, Tony Wendice, is a retired tennis champion. Michael Douglas and Gwyneth Paltrow's characters are also shown as a very wealthy couple. Both Kelly and Paltrow's characters are striking blondes. Both films make use of the mystery of the fact that no key was found on the dead man when he was killed by Kelly and Paltrow's characters, as both their husbands had removed them in an attempt to pin the crime on their wives. Toward the beginning of ''Dial M for Murder'', when Kelly and [[Robert Cummings]] are shown together in the Wendice flat, and Milland comes home, Kelly greets him with "There you are!" and kisses him. Presumably in homage to the original film, Douglas's character greets Paltrow exactly the same way when she arrives home to their apartment at the beginning of ''A Perfect Murder''. Throughout the film, Emily carries an Hermès Kelly bag, named after Grace Kelly who was often photographed carrying the model of purse. The title ''A Perfect Murder'' matches the translation that was made in some countries of Hitchcock's film, known in Italian as ''Il delitto perfetto'' and in Spanish as ''Crimen perfecto''; in French it was ''Le crime était presque parfait.'' ==Production== In June 1997, it was reported that [[Michael Douglas]] and director [[Andrew Davis (director)|Andrew Davis]] were in negotiations with [[Warner Bros. Pictures|Warner Bros.]] to team on ''A Perfect Murder'', a loose remake of ''[[Dial M for Murder]]'' for producers [[Arnold Kopelson|Arnold and Anne Kopelson]].{{cite news|url= https://variety.com/1997/film/news/douglas-davis-talking-murder-1116679053/|title= Douglas, Davis talking ‘Murder’ |publisher=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date= November 11, 2025 |archive-date= November 11, 2025 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20251111035453/http://web.archive.org/screenshot/https://variety.com/1997/film/news/douglas-davis-talking-murder-1116679053/}} In August of that year, [[Gwyneth Paltrow]] joined the cast opposite Douglas.{{cite news|url= https://variety.com/1997/film/news/paltrow-plans-for-murder-at-warners-1116678688/|title= Paltrow plans for ‘Murder’at Warners |publisher=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date= November 11, 2025 |archive-date= January 26, 2022 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220126183647/https://variety.com/1997/film/news/paltrow-plans-for-murder-at-warners-1116678688/}} Principal photography began on October 14, 1997. Filming took place in & around [[New York City]]. The location of Steven & Emily's apartment was filmed at the [[Convent of the Sacred Heart (New York City)|Convent of the Sacred Heart]] building in Manhattan. The Bradford Mansion was filmed at the [[Salutation (estate)|Salutation House]] in [[Long Island]]. Filming ended on January 13, 1998. ==Alternate ending== An alternate ending exists and is presented, with optional commentary, on the original Blu-ray disc release.{{cite web|last1=Douglas|first1=Clark|title=''A Perfect Murder'' (Blu-ray)|url=http://www.dvdverdict.com/reviews/perfectmurderbluray.php|website=[[DVD Verdict]]|access-date=10 November 2015|date=July 30, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151127161208/http://www.dvdverdict.com/reviews/perfectmurderbluray.php|archive-date=27 November 2015}}{{cite web|title=''A Perfect Murder'' [Blu-ray]|url=https://www.amazon.ca/A-Perfect-Murder-Blu-ray-Bilingual/dp/B008N8A3EY|website=[[Amazon.ca]]|date=17 July 2012 |publisher=amazon.ca|access-date=10 November 2015}} In this version, Steven comes back from finding the key replaced where he had hidden it and Emily confronts him in the kitchen rather than in their foyer. The scene plays out with the same dialogue, but Steven never physically attacks her. He still tells her that the only way she'll leave him is dead, and she shoots him. Steven then says "You won't get away with this" before dying and Emily purposely injures herself, making it look like self-defense. ==Reception== ===Box office=== ''A Perfect Murder'' opened in second place at the [[box office]] behind ''[[The Truman Show]]'', grossing $16,615,704 during its first weekend. It ended with a total worldwide gross of $128,038,368.{{mojo title|perfectmurder|A Perfect Murder}} ===Critical response=== ''A Perfect Murder'' received mixed reviews. [[Stephen Holden]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' called it a "skillfully plotted update of Frederick Knott's play".{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/06/05/movies/film-review-perfect-plan-kill-my-wife-please.html |newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|title=Film Review – ''A Perfect Murder''|first=Stephen|last=Holden|author-link=Stephen Holden|date=5 June 1998| access-date=2 January 2017}} [[Owen Gleiberman]] of ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' commented, "I've seen far worse thrillers than ''A Perfect Murder'', but the movie is finally more competent than it is pleasurable. All that lingers from it is the color of money."{{cite magazine|last1=Gleiberman|first1=Owen|author-link=Owen Gleiberman|title=''A Perfect Murder''|url=https://ew.com/article/1998/06/12/perfect-murder-3/ |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|access-date=September 20, 2025|date=June 12, 1998}} Rita Kempley of ''[[The Washington Post]]'' noted, "The trouble is, we don't really much care about this philandering billionaire glamour puss, who seems perfectly capable of taking care of herself. We don't care about her husband or lover either. The story's most compelling character, an Arab American detective (the superb British actor David Suchet), becomes a minor player here. Nevertheless, like John Williams in the Hitchcock film, Suchet commits the film's only believable crime: He steals the show."{{cite news |last1=Kempley |first1=Rita |title='A Perfect Murder': Dial M for Mediocre |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/style/longterm/movies/videos/perfectmurderkempley.htm |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=31 August 2020 |date=5 June 1998}} [[Paul Clinton]] of [[CNN]] observed, "This production is stylishly mounted... Douglas is an excellent actor and a gifted producer. However, he should hang up his spurs when it comes to playing a romantic lead with women in their twenties."{{cite web |last1=Clinton |first1=Paul |title=Review: ''A Perfect Murder'' full of flaws|url=http://edition.cnn.com/SHOWBIZ/Movies/9806/04/perfect.murder.review/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040208003342/http://edition.cnn.com/SHOWBIZ/Movies/9806/04/perfect.murder.review/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 8, 2004|publisher=[[CNN]] |access-date=31 August 2020 |date=4 June 1998}} [[Roger Ebert]], who gave the film three stars out of four, wrote "[It] works like a nasty little machine to keep us involved and disturbed; my attention never strayed".{{cite news| url=http://rogerebert.suntimes.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/19980605/REVIEWS/806050301/1023|newspaper=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=[[Roger Ebert]]|title=Reviews – ''A Perfect Murder''| access-date=2010-07-05| archive-date=2012-10-08| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121008224905/http://rogerebert.suntimes.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=%2F19980605%2FREVIEWS%2F806050301%2F1023| url-status=dead}} Meanwhile, [[James Berardinelli]] wrote that the film "has inexplicably managed to eliminate almost everything that was worthwhile about ''Dial M for Murder'', leaving behind the nearly-unwatchable wreckage of a would-be '90s thriller."{{cite news |last=Berardinelli |first=James |date=1998 |title=Review: A Perfect Number |url=http://preview.reelviews.net/movies/p/perfect_murder.html |website=ReelViews.net}} ''A Perfect Murder'' holds a 55% rating on [[Rotten Tomatoes]] from 55 reviews. The site's consensus states: "A slick little thriller that relies a bit too much on surprise events to generate suspense."{{cite web|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/1083171-perfect_murder|website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]|title=''A Perfect Murder''}} It has a score of 50/100, based on 22 reviews ("mixed or average" reviews) from [[Metacritic]].{{cite web|url=http://www.metacritic.com/movie/a-perfect-murder|website=[[Metacritic]]|title=Film Review – ''A Perfect Murder''}} Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B" on an A+ to F scale.{{Cite web |title=Cinemascore |url=https://www.cinemascore.com/publicsearch/index/title/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181220122629/https://www.cinemascore.com/publicsearch/index/title/ |archive-date=2018-12-20}} ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== {{Portal|United States|1990s|Film}} * {{IMDb title|0120787}} * {{Metacritic film|A Perfect Murder}} * {{TCMDb title|327368}} * {{mojo title|perfectmurder}} * {{Rotten-tomatoes|1083171-perfect_murder}} {{Andrew Davis}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Perfect Murder, A}} [[Category:1998 films]] [[Category:1998 English-language films]] [[Category:1990s erotic thriller films]] [[Category:1998 crime thriller films]] [[Category:American films based on plays]] [[Category:Remakes of American films]] [[Category:American crime thriller films]] [[Category:Films about adultery in the United States]] [[Category:Films about con artists]] [[Category:Films about contract killing in the United States]] [[Category:Films directed by Andrew Davis]] [[Category:Films produced by Arnold Kopelson]] [[Category:Films scored by James Newton Howard]] [[Category:Films set in Brooklyn]] [[Category:Films set in Manhattan]] [[Category:Films shot in New York City]] [[Category:Warner Bros. films]] [[Category:Films produced by Peter MacGregor-Scott]] [[Category:1998 American films]] [[Category:English-language crime thriller films]] [[Category:1998 erotic films]]
